s_open.name: 15:00, Wednesday
s_open.title: 15:00, Wednesday
s_open.body:
You are covering a shift for Danni, who called in sick.

Rachael, 24. She works Wednesdays at a garden centre on the north side of town. The roster says collect her at 3:00 and drive her to physio at 3:30.

This is your first shift with her. Her photo is on her profile, so you know who you are looking for. You are parked where you can see the front doors of the garden centre.

It is three o'clock. You decide to check the previous shift worker's note for this morning's shift.

s_note.name: The note
s_note.title: Last Wednesday's note
s_note.body: Took Rachael to work. All good. She was a little fidgety on the way but we talked about music and she relaxed a bit.

q_arrive.name: She doesn't come out
q_arrive.title: Nobody comes out
q_arrive.body:
Ten past three. Staff come and go through the front doors. None of them is Rachael.

Physio is a twelve minute drive and they give fifteen minutes' grace. Your next client is at four, across town.

What do you do?

choices.label: Go in and ask a staff member to find her
Log a no-show and get to your next client

s_ask.name: You go in and ask
s_ask.title: You go in and ask
s_ask.body:
The woman on the register is helpful. She picks up the handset behind the counter.

"Rachael to the front counter please, Rachael to the front counter, your lift is here."

It carries the length of the shop. A bloke stacking mulch looks up. Two customers in the queue look up.

Someone goes out the back to fetch her, and she comes the whole way through the shop to the front counter, past the registers, past the queue, with her bag on her shoulder.

She does not look at you until you are both outside.

You make physio with three minutes to spare.

s_ring.name: You ring the office
s_ring.title: You ring the office
s_ring.body:
It rings out. You leave a message.

Nobody at the office knows where Rachael waits either. It was never written down, so there is nothing in the file for them to read back to you even if they answer.

Rachael rang them nine minutes ago from the pallet by the loading door, wondering where her lift was. That message is sitting under yours.

It is 3:18. You are still in the car park.

s_wait.name: You both wait
s_wait.title: You wait. So does she.
s_wait.body:
You wait in the car. Rachael waits on a pallet by the loading door, where she waits every Wednesday.

At half past three she gives up and walks round to the front.

Physio is gone. You ring them from the car park and rebook for Tuesday.

She does not say anything on the drive home. When you ask if she is alright she says she is fine.

s_noshow.name: You log a no-show
s_noshow.title: You log it as a no-show
s_noshow.body:
It is the defensible call. You waited ten minutes, she did not come out, and you have a client at four.

You tap client not present and drive across town.

Rachael sat on the pallet until twenty to four. Then she walked home, because the office had not picked up and she did not have your number.

She was there the whole time.

The file now says she was not. At her next plan review, that is one more line saying this support is not being used.

q_note.name: Your turn to write
q_note.title: You are writing your own note now
q_note.body:
Next Wednesday somebody covers Rachael. It might be Danni. It might be someone who has never met her.

Which of these would you write?

choices.label: "Collected Rachael from work and drove her to physio. All went well."
choices.feedback: "All went well" is your judgement, and the next worker cannot act on it. They will sit in that car park watching the front doors exactly like you did.

choices.label: "Rachael works in the back and waits by the loading door when she finishes, not the front entrance. She'd rather not be collected where the shop can see. Collected her at 3:12."
choices.feedback: This is the one — and the second sentence is the half that matters. Where she waits saves the next worker ten minutes. Why she waits there stops them deciding the front would be simpler and asking her to move.

choices.label: "Rachael wasn't waiting where she was supposed to be."
choices.feedback: "Supposed to be" makes it Rachael's error. She was exactly where she always is. The only thing that was not where it should have been is the information.

s_end.name: Debrief
s_end.title: There was no good option at ten past three
s_end.body:
The roster was right. You were on time. Rachael finished when she always finishes and waited where she always waits.

Every option cost her something.

Asking inside got her to physio — and walked her the length of the shop past the registers, which is the exact thing she goes out the back to avoid. Waiting cost her the appointment. The office could not help, because nobody had written it down for them either. And a no-show put something in her file that was not true.

Danni never wrote it down. Danni just goes round the back. After a few months it became an unremarkable habit, so it did not get written.

This is the trap — notes that feel unremarkable to you could be essential in ways we can't predict.

Here is the note that would have prevented all of it:

Drove Rachael to the garden centre for her 9:00 start. She works in the back and waits by the loading door when she finishes, not the front entrance — she would rather not be collected where the shop can see. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio.

This note takes a couple of minutes to write, and it could have saved Rachael so much.

A note is not for you. It is for the day you are not there.

s_profile.name: Her profile
s_profile.title: You open her profile
s_profile.body:
While you wait, you open Rachael's profile on the app.

It is a good file. Service agreement, current plan, physio referral — all dated this year.

Goals. Keep working Wednesdays at the garden centre. Finish the physio program on her left shoulder. Build up to using the bus on her own.

Risks & Health. Shoulder injury in July. No medications. No allergies.

Rachael can find busy or crowded environments difficult.

You put your phone down and watch the doors.
